summary: Backend-only test for the NEW long-press drag-to-reorder FEATURE — PATCH /api/programs/{pid}/sessions/{sid}/exercises/{eid}/order now accepts {"newIndex": N} in addition to legacy {"direction": "up|down"}. All 14 tests PASS against live backend using user_b@theprogram.app (52-week Hypertrophy plan). Covers: (1) multi-position jump (first→last in one call); (2) isolation — other display groups' orders untouched; (3) propagation to current+future weeks of same sessionType, past bit-for-bit untouched; (4a) newIndex<0 clamps to 0; (4b) newIndex>=groupLen clamps to last; (4c) newIndex==current is no-op; (5a-c) 400 on string/bool newIndex and empty body; (5d) 404 on unknown exerciseId; (6a-c) REGRESSION — direction=up/down still swap with adjacent in-group neighbor, section-edge is no-op, invalid direction w/o newIndex → 400; (7) duplicate-name tiebreaker verified via code review (endpoint uses target_group_pos when future session has same-name+same-category matches; branch active for newIndex mode). Also confirmed prior 8/8 isolated-reorder tests still pass — no regression. Every mutating test reverts its DB change; user's plan is preserved for native drag-UX testing.

test_results.test_1_multi_position_jump_first_to_last: PASS — target moved 0→last in ONE call; group id-sequence rearranged correctly; order pool preserved; non-group exercises untouched; reverted
test_results.test_2_isolation_other_groups_unaffected: PASS — jumping within one display group leaves every other group's {id→order} snapshot bit-identical
test_results.test_3_propagation_future_weeks_swapped_: PASS — past_before==past_after; future weeks show same-named target at last position; updatedSessions>=1; reverted
test_results.test_4a_clamp_negative_to_zero: PASS — newIndex=-5 lands target at group[0]; response echoes newIndex:-5 (clamping is internal, as expected)
test_results.test_4b_clamp_overflow_to_last: PASS — newIndex=len+99 lands target at group[-1]
test_results.test_4c_current_position_is_noop: PASS — newIndex==current_idx keeps target session's {id→order} identical
test_results.test_5b_newindex_boolean_returns_400: PASS — isinstance(bool) explicitly excluded in endpoint
test_results.test_5c_empty_body_returns_400: PASS — {} → 400 with 'direction must be up/down or provide newIndex'
test_results.test_6a_direction_up_swaps_adjacent: PASS — legacy path unchanged; response now includes newIndex:null
test_results.test_6b_direction_edge_noop: PASS — first-in-group UP still a no-op
test_results.test_7_disambiguation_code_review: PASS — target_group_pos + 'if len(matches) > 1 and target_group_pos in matches' present; newIndex clamp expression 'max(0, min(new_index, len(group) - 1))' present; past-week skip intact
test_results.regression_test_reorder_isolated.py: PASS 8/8 — no regression on prior isolated-reorder tests

critical_code_review_comments: Endpoint /app/backend/server.py:866-984 cleanly accepts EITHER newIndex OR direction. Validation at line 876-880 correctly rejects bool via isinstance(new_index, bool) check.

newIndex branch (lines 962-971) uses in-place pop/insert on the group list and reassigns order values from a pre-collected ascending order_pool — this preserves the exact order-value spacing of the group even when it's non-contiguous (e.g. warmup=1,2 / main=10,20,30).
target_group_pos disambiguation (lines 924-928, 955-956) applies to BOTH newIndex and direction modes — correctly handles same-name+same-category duplicates in future sessions.
Past-week skip guard (line 934) unchanged — past weeks remain bit-identical after any move.
In-memory cache invalidation (line 980) still in place — subsequent GET /api/plan/year returns fresh state.
Response contract at line 983-984 correctly returns null for the mode not used ({direction: null, newIndex: N} for newIndex path; {direction: 'up', newIndex: None} for direction path).
seed_data_creation: None — used user_b@theprogram.app's existing 52-week Hypertrophy plan. Fixture selects a ≥3-exercise display group with distinct order values + future weeks of same sessionType. Every mutating test reverts its change so DB is preserved for native drag-UX testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The reorder endpoint now supports both {newIndex:N} (absolute position, clamped) and {direction:'up'|'down'} (legacy adjacent swap). Both paths share the same display-group isolation, current+future-week propagation, past-week protection, and duplicate-name tiebreaker (target_group_pos). Fixture in test_reorder_new_index.py requires a ≥3-exercise display group with distinct orders and at least one future-week session of the same sessionType — user_b (52-wk Hypertrophy) satisfies this. Boundary case 2 (natural same-name+same-category duplicates in a future session's group) has no natural fixture in current seed data; disambiguation was verified via code review only. If needed later, insert a synthetic duplicate directly into db.saved_plans to exercise the runtime branch.
rca_of_issue: No issue found. The newIndex extension is behaviorally correct across all tested paths (isolation, propagation, clamping, no-op, validation) and the legacy direction path is a clean regression pass.
